Technical Project Delivery

Quality, Testing & Documentation

Client & Cross-Functional Partnership

•    5+ recent years of directly relevant technical project management experience, managing technical web development, infrastructure, and support projects in an Agile environment.

•    Experience managing the development of government agency websites, web applications, or secure portals.

•    Proficiency with Google Analytics, modern PM tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence), and familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, Git version control, and API integrations.
•    Positive attitude, highly collaborative, friendly, and deadline-driven.

★ PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

•    PMI Certification (PMP, PMI-ACP), Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), or formal project management training.
•    Experience with government contracting environments.

BrightLeaf Group is an Austin-based digital transformation firm with 34+ years serving state and local government agencies. We specialize in web applications, accessibility, EXP platforms, and strategic digital communications — and we take quality seriously.
This is an opportunity to lead technically complex, mission-driven projects and work alongside a focused, expert delivery practice.

•    Remote-first work with an Austin, Texas home base for periodic team and client connection.
•    Competitive compensation commensurate with experience.

Company Description

We believe in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies, and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams of experts combine innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to progress further, faster. Our clients adapt and transform, and together we achieve enduring results.

We are over 4,000 strategists, innovators, designers, consultants, digital experts, scientists, engineers, and technologists. And we have deep expertise in consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences, and transport.

Our teams operate globally from offices across the UK, Ireland, US, Nordics, and Netherlands.

PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life

Job Description

This practice is built for the way enterprise software actually gets made now: small senior pods, AI agents doing much of the build, and outcomes in weeks where traditional delivery approaches took months. We build digital products, AI agents, intelligent workflows and modernized platforms that help organizations operate differently across healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, energy and utilities, transportation and consumer industries. None of it is pilots or demos. The solutions we build run in production and solve problems that matter to our clients' businesses.

As a Product Strategist, you'll help clients identify which problems are worth solving and shape products that deliver measurable value. Working alongside AI Engineers and Data Engineers, you'll take opportunities from discovery through adoption, combining deep business understanding with a practical view of what technology can achieve. The person defining the product is also accountable for whether it gets used, which means you'll stay close to the outcome long after launch.

This role sits at the intersection of business, technology, and delivery. AI agents are changing how products are built, but they cannot decide what should be built in the first place. You'll work through ambiguity, challenge assumptions, and help clients move from broad ambitions to solutions that create lasting impact.

As part of the Digital Products & AI team, you can expect to:

Lead discovery with clients to understand how work gets done, where value is being lost, and which opportunities are worth pursuing.
Define product requirements, priorities, acceptance criteria, and success measures that guide delivery and enable measurable outcomes.
Translate business challenges into products, AI-enabled solutions, and intelligent workflows that people will trust and adopt.
Shape how AI capabilities are applied, including what should be automated, where human oversight is required, and how success should be evaluated.
Drive adoption by aligning stakeholders, supporting change, and helping clients redesign processes where necessary to realize value.
Create reusable approaches, assets, and industry insights that strengthen future engagements, with the strongest ideas becoming capabilities and offerings we take to market.

Qualifications

Product and strategy foundations

Experience leading discovery, shaping product direction, and translating complex business challenges into actionable plans.
Experience building business cases, defining success measures, and demonstrating value realization.

Industry and AI understanding

Deep expertise in at least one industry sector, with the ability to quickly establish credibility with both operational and executive stakeholders.
Working knowledge of AI-enabled products, including agents, retrieval approaches, automation, and the opportunities and limitations of modern AI systems.
Experience evaluating competing opportunities and making informed decisions about where technology can create the greatest impact.

Enterprise delivery

Experience working with multidisciplinary teams to deliver technology solutions from concept through implementation and adoption.
Strong communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and influence decisions across multiple levels of an organization.
Commercial judgment and the ability to balance business value, user needs, technical feasibility, and delivery constraints.

Ideally, you'll also bring:

Experience delivering solutions within consulting, professional services, or a leadership role within your industry.
Experience in healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, energy and utilities, transportation, or consumer industries.
Experience with change management, operating model design, process transformation, or driving adoption of new technologies.
Experience using data, analytics, AI tools, SQL, Python, or similar approaches to support decision-making and product strategy.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
What This Role Is

Every year, hundreds of thousands of students across India decide they want to study abroad. Some come through K12 school partnerships, some find their way in directly. Either way, they enter a journey - discovery, counseling, application, offer, enrollment - that runs through dozens of handoffs between people, platforms, and teams. When that journey works, a student ends up at a university that fits their budget, their course, and their ambitions, and the business realizes revenue at the moment they enroll. When it doesn't, applications stall, deadlines slip, and a student who could have enrolled goes quiet.

The problem is not that any single team is failing. It's that the highest-leverage work in a business like this doesn't live inside one function - it lives in the transformation and optimization projects that cut across Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations, and someone needs to own them end to end. A funnel improvement that Marketing wants tested needs Product to build it and Tech to ship it. A new process that could remove a structural inefficiency needs someone to design it, prove it, and hand it off cleanly. Right now, that ownership happens informally, project by project, and the work that would compound doesn't get the sustained, disciplined execution it needs.

This is where this role sits. You will run multiple 'Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer' projects a year - some of them genuinely 0-1 (new ideas that need user research, market research, and hypothesis testing before anyone knows if they work), some of them optimization projects on things that already exist but need better process design and a new benchmark for what good looks like. You will also be asked to take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even when it doesn't have a job title yet.

You will own full-cycle delivery for these projects - from framing the problem with the right stakeholders, through build and testing, to launch, operating it long enough to prove it works, and transferring it cleanly to whoever owns it long-term. You are the person who makes sure a project doesn't just get discussed. It gets shipped, it gets proven, and it gets handed off in a state someone else can run with.

What Makes This Role Different

Most program management roles ask you to track a roadmap someone else designed. This one asks you to build the roadmap itself - deciding what the next transformation or optimization project should even be, then owning it across three or four functions that don't naturally report to the same person. The Strategize-Build-Operate-Transfer model means you don't hand a project off the moment it launches; you stay accountable until it's actually working and someone else can run it without you.

The Manifest ecosystem gives this role real range: some projects will be genuinely 0-1 - a new idea nobody has tested yet - and others will be 1-100 - scaling something that already works but is starting to strain under its own complexity. Few program roles at this stage give you exposure to both ends of that spectrum in the same year.

This is a build role, not a maintenance one. There is no finished playbook for how these projects should run - you're expected to design the frameworks, set the benchmarks, and prove through disciplined experimentation what should scale and what shouldn't.

What You Own

Transformation projects (Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer)

Translate a business problem into a project plan that Tech, Product, Marketing and Business teams can actually execute against
Own the full lifecycle of assigned projects - scoping, stakeholder alignment, build, testing, launch, and post-launch review
Own multiple SBOT-cycle projects a year, end to end, from initial strategy through a clean operational handoff
Define what "operate" looks like well enough to prove a project works before transferring ownership
Ensure nothing gets handed off half-finished - the transfer is only complete when the receiving team can run it without you

0-1 initiatives

Lead user research, market research, and hypothesis testing on new ideas before committing resources to build them
Design and run experiments that give a clear read on whether an idea is worth scaling
Turn ambiguous, early-stage problems into a testable plan within weeks, not quarters

Optimization and process design

Identify structural inefficiencies across the business and turn them into scoped optimization projects
Build the frameworks and process designs that make a function run better, not just faster
Set new benchmarks for what "good" looks like once a process has been redesigned

Cross-functional execution and influence

Be the connective layer between Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations so a project doesn't stall in the gap between roadmaps
Lead cross-functional execution through credibility, influence, and clear decision-making rather than formal authority
Take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even without a predefined mandate

What Success Looks Like

The markers below reflect where Student Placements is today. We'll calibrate the specifics once you're in the seat. These are directional, not fixed.

In your first weeks, you're not shipping yet - you're building a working map of how projects actually move through Tech, Product, and Marketing today, and forming a point of view on where the highest-leverage transformation or optimization opportunities sit. You'll know you're on track when stakeholders start coming to you before a project stalls, not after.

By the middle of your first year, you've run at least one full SBOT cycle from strategy to clean handoff, and the people around you trust that if you've said something will happen, it will. You've proven, through real experiments rather than opinion, which 0-1 ideas are worth scaling and which aren't.

Longer term, the way the business runs cross-functional projects looks different because you built it that way - frameworks that outlast the specific projects they were built for, a track record of transformations that actually stuck, and a reputation as the person who gets called in when something critical and undefined needs to happen.

What This Role Is

Every year, hundreds of thousands of students across India decide they want to study abroad. Some come through K12 school partnerships, some find their way in directly. Either way, they enter a journey - discovery, counseling, application, offer, enrollment - that runs through dozens of handoffs between people, platforms, and teams. When that journey works, a student ends up at a university that fits their budget, their course, and their ambitions, and the business realizes revenue at the moment they enroll. When it doesn't, applications stall, deadlines slip, and a student who could have enrolled goes quiet.

The problem is not that any single team is failing. It's that the highest-leverage work in a business like this doesn't live inside one function - it lives in the transformation and optimization projects that cut across Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations, and someone needs to own them end to end. A funnel improvement that Marketing wants tested needs Product to build it and Tech to ship it. A new process that could remove a structural inefficiency needs someone to design it, prove it, and hand it off cleanly. Right now, that ownership happens informally, project by project, and the work that would compound doesn't get the sustained, disciplined execution it needs.

This is where this role sits. You will run multiple 'Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer' projects a year - some of them genuinely 0-1 (new ideas that need user research, market research, and hypothesis testing before anyone knows if they work), some of them optimization projects on things that already exist but need better process design and a new benchmark for what good looks like. You will also be asked to take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even when it doesn't have a job title yet.

You will own full-cycle delivery for these projects - from framing the problem with the right stakeholders, through build and testing, to launch, operating it long enough to prove it works, and transferring it cleanly to whoever owns it long-term. You are the person who makes sure a project doesn't just get discussed. It gets shipped, it gets proven, and it gets handed off in a state someone else can run with.

What Makes This Role Different

Most program management roles ask you to track a roadmap someone else designed. This one asks you to build the roadmap itself - deciding what the next transformation or optimization project should even be, then owning it across three or four functions that don't naturally report to the same person. The Strategize-Build-Operate-Transfer model means you don't hand a project off the moment it launches; you stay accountable until it's actually working and someone else can run it without you.

The Manifest ecosystem gives this role real range: some projects will be genuinely 0-1 - a new idea nobody has tested yet - and others will be 1-100 - scaling something that already works but is starting to strain under its own complexity. Few program roles at this stage give you exposure to both ends of that spectrum in the same year.

This is a build role, not a maintenance one. There is no finished playbook for how these projects should run - you're expected to design the frameworks, set the benchmarks, and prove through disciplined experimentation what should scale and what shouldn't.

What You Own

Transformation projects (Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer)

Translate a business problem into a project plan that Tech, Product, Marketing and Business teams can actually execute against
Own the full lifecycle of assigned projects - scoping, stakeholder alignment, build, testing, launch, and post-launch review
Own multiple SBOT-cycle projects a year, end to end, from initial strategy through a clean operational handoff
Define what "operate" looks like well enough to prove a project works before transferring ownership
Ensure nothing gets handed off half-finished - the transfer is only complete when the receiving team can run it without you

0-1 initiatives

Lead user research, market research, and hypothesis testing on new ideas before committing resources to build them
Design and run experiments that give a clear read on whether an idea is worth scaling
Turn ambiguous, early-stage problems into a testable plan within weeks, not quarters

Optimization and process design

Identify structural inefficiencies across the business and turn them into scoped optimization projects
Build the frameworks and process designs that make a function run better, not just faster
Set new benchmarks for what "good" looks like once a process has been redesigned

Cross-functional execution and influence

Be the connective layer between Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations so a project doesn't stall in the gap between roadmaps
Lead cross-functional execution through credibility, influence, and clear decision-making rather than formal authority
Take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even without a predefined mandate

What Success Looks Like

The markers below reflect where Student Placements is today. We'll calibrate the specifics once you're in the seat. These are directional, not fixed.

In your first weeks, you're not shipping yet - you're building a working map of how projects actually move through Tech, Product, and Marketing today, and forming a point of view on where the highest-leverage transformation or optimization opportunities sit. You'll know you're on track when stakeholders start coming to you before a project stalls, not after.

By the middle of your first year, you've run at least one full SBOT cycle from strategy to clean handoff, and the people around you trust that if you've said something will happen, it will. You've proven, through real experiments rather than opinion, which 0-1 ideas are worth scaling and which aren't.

Longer term, the way the business runs cross-functional projects looks different because you built it that way - frameworks that outlast the specific projects they were built for, a track record of transformations that actually stuck, and a reputation as the person who gets called in when something critical and undefined needs to happen.

The specifics will be calibrated once you're in the role. The direction won't change.

What You Bring

You've spent five to eight years building things inside high-growth environments, and you've likely seen both ends of that growth curve - the 0-1 phase, where the job is rapid experimentation, hypothesis testing, and getting an MVP in front of real users, and the 1-100 phase, where the job becomes process design and managing the complexity that scale creates. You know which mode a problem calls for and you don't try to apply 1-100 rigor to a 0-1 problem, or vice versa.

You have real comfort operating in ambiguity, and more than that, you're fast at moving from ambiguity to clarity - you ask the right question early, you don't wait for someone to hand you a clean brief, and you get to a workable answer quickly rather than a perfect one slowly.

You think in first principles. When a process is broken, you don't default to the existing framework - you rebuild the logic from the ground up and design something better, then prove it works before asking anyone to trust it.

Most importantly, you read the description of what this role is building and your first reaction was not "this sounds like a coordination job." It was "this is exactly the kind of ambiguous, high-leverage problem I want to be handed." That's the person this role is for.

Why Manifest

Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility - connecting students, schools, universities, and employers across 50+ countries. Our portfolio spans Cialfo (AI-powered college counseling, 2,000+ schools), BridgeU (university guidance for international schools globally), Kaaiser (trusted study abroad counseling since 1997 across India and Southeast Asia), and Explore (AI-powered university outreach, 1,000+ university partners). Together, we move talent across borders at scale. $700B flows annually in remittances from migrant workers. 85M workers will be missing from developed economies by 2030. We're building the operating system which changes that. $80M raised. Still early.

Student Placements is where that infrastructure meets an individual student's decision - and the transformation and optimization work this role owns is what makes that infrastructure work better at every scale it operates at.

Description

TL;DR
Kharon is seeking a full-time, in-office Research Analyst, Data Operations with working proficiency in a Mandarin (simplified and/or traditional), to join our team in Washington D.C. This role requires in office attendance.

Kharon is a highly disruptive and incredibly innovative organization that navigates risk at the intersection of global security threats + international commerce.

What does that mean? Great question.

Operating at the nexus of global security, Kharon is on a mission to revolutionize the current landscape. We take really complex data as it relates to global security and empower our clients to not only understand the risk associated with their potential business relationships but to operationalize that data so that they can make the best and most informed decisions possible. From financial crimes and sanctions to export controls and threat identifications, our tools optimize protection against the types of risks that could otherwise be incredibly dangerous and excessively costly to any business. Serving many of today’s leading global financial and multinational institutions, Kharon products are the most powerful in the space with a precision and depth that is absolutely unparalleled.

When you look at any major global crisis event, we’re providing intelligence that’s at the heart of those circumstances. We connect the dots in a way that’s meaningful. Now, we’re experiencing unprecedented growth. As the world continues to evolve in complexity, so too does the demand for our products. Given the significance of our work and the increasing global reliance on our insights, we are looking for a Director of Growth Marketing to join us as we work to shape the way businesses perceive and navigate global risks.

Reporting to the Associate Director of Data Operations, the core of this position is dedicated to conducting open-source research on a variety of foreign affairs and national security issues. More specifically, you will be researching, analyzing, and interpreting data as it relates to sanctions, export controls, and criminal/illicit networks. You will be responsible for the diligent pursuit of data as it relates to ever-evolving market demand and our client inquiries. Working collaboratively with the Kharon Research team, you will contribute to the development of new datasets and update existing ones, identifying and utilizing new sources and developing subject matter expertise on the various strategic topics. This includes monitoring new sanctions, enforcement actions, and policy activity by regulatory agencies, as well as conducting research on international affairs that affect business risks. Leveraging your sound analytical approach and research techniques, you will identify data typologies, perform detailed quality assurance, validate and reconcile data, and support new product and partnership initiatives. You’ll also play a key role in curating, publishing, and maintaining datasets, and may write original code to collect primary data across various languages. Cross-functional collaboration is essential as you help build out new research, surface insights from existing content, and report key project metrics to internal stakeholders.

To the right person, this will be the perfect kind of challenge. Our mission is compelling, our product is powerful, and we’re growing at a rate that makes us unstoppable. If you’re looking to be surrounded by people who will inspire you to think and challenge you to grow then look no further. Our team is made up of some of the most visionary and uncompromising individuals you will ever encounter. We don’t take ourselves seriously but we’re serious about the work we do and there is absolutely no slowing us down.

Responsibilities

Monitoring new sanctions, enforcement actions, and policy activity by regulatory agencies for developments relevant to Kharon’s products
Conducting research on issues in international affairs that impact business risks and identifying relevant data sources
Driving the curation, publication, maintenance, and quality assurance of datasets
Performing data validation and reconciliation to support new products and partnership initiatives
Accurately perform detailed quality assurance of data and developing additional tooling to support these tasks as necessary
Write original code needed to collect primary data in any number of different languages.
Collaborating cross-functionally to build out new research and develop insights based on Kharon’s existing content
Reporting key metrics on projects and share regular updates with stakeholders.

Qualifications

Must have a Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Business Administration, International Relations, Political Science, Security Studies, Regional Studies, History, Sociology, or a related field
Experience with sanctions, export controls, anti-money laundering or countering the financing of terrorism
Experience researching issues of international security and economy in high-risk jurisdictions
Understanding of securities markets, financial instruments, and investment risk
Must have working reading proficiency in Mandarin.
2+ years experience in coding languages (Python strongly preferred)
1+ year experience in using scraping and data parsing packages (e.g., Selenium, Scrapy, proxies, Captcha BeautifulSoup, pandas, etc.)
Experience with or willingness to learn SQL
Experience with data analysis, data visualization, and graph databases (Neo4J)
Understanding of or willingness to learn web technologies (HTML, JavaScript, CSS, XPath, JSON, etc).

Benefits

To keep that momentum going, we do our very best to make sure that each and every team member is completely taken care of. We’re nothing without our people and we strive to offer a package that reflects that. As a Kharon team member, you can expect:

Fully sponsored medical, dental, and vision insurances
FSA program for both medical and dependent care
401k + Roth with matching and immediate vesting
Flexible paid time off + 11 paid holidays

The base salary range at Kharon is set between $68,000-$78,000. Please note that this figure does not necessarily include potential bonuses, commissions, benefits, or equity that may be part of the overall compensation package.
